hypothesis: Exhaustively extend the registered finite equal-weight formula grammar from eight to nine prior-only features. Test whether the added feature yields a stable rank-hit improvement relative to the eight-feature formula selected by the same discovery/validation rule. No new feature definitions or tuning are introduced. Formula-family results remain exploratory; a single candidate is frozen using discovery and validation only before its blind OOS evaluation.

formula_universe.enumeration: lexicographic itertools.combinations over the registered 27 prior-only feature columns
formula_universe.shard_partition: contiguous lexicographic formula-rank intervals; every rank 0..4686824 appears exactly once, no gaps or overlaps

walk_forward.split_rule: discovery if target_offset/scored_targets < 0.60; validation if <0.80; else blind_oos
walk_forward.prior_only_cutoff: For target archive index i, every feature uses draws[0:i] only; record cutoff date i-1; rank all 40 numbers before reading/scoring target i; update state only after scoring.
walk_forward.scoring_rule: z-score each of the 27 registered features across numbers 1..40 for each target prefix; score each unordered nine-feature subset by the equal-weight arithmetic mean of its nine standardized feature columns
walk_forward.retrospective_best_formula: Descriptive only; never use as an ex-ante forecast or candidate-selection rule.

multiple_testing.method: Global Holm-Bonferroni across the complete registered formula×split×primary-endpoint family
multiple_testing.p_value_method: Finite-population null: for each target, the five actual distinct numbers are a uniform 5-subset of 40, so X_k~Hypergeometric(N=40,K=k,n=5); aggregate mean/variance across split targets and use a continuity-corrected normal upper-tail approximation. Exploratory approximation, not an exact p-value.
multiple_testing.dependency_note: Holm controls family-wise error under arbitrary dependence if input p-values are valid; the normal approximation and lottery-independence assumptions remain limitations.

frozen_candidate_selection.rule: Select the top 100 nine-feature formulas on Discovery by mean number_hits_top5, tie-break by lower mean_rank_of_actual_numbers, then lexicographic formula_id. From those 100, select exactly one on Validation by mean number_hits_top5 with the same tie-break. Do not use Blind OOS values, retrospective per-target winners, or blind top lists to select the candidate.
frozen_candidate_selection.eight_feature_control: Apply the identical top-100 Discovery then single-candidate Validation rule to the refreshed Q88 eight-feature metrics on the same archive and splits. Freeze both IDs before blind evaluation.
frozen_candidate_selection.blind_primary_comparison: Paired difference in number_hits_top5 per target between the frozen nine-feature candidate and frozen eight-feature control over the 670 blind OOS targets.
frozen_candidate_selection.inference: For the three paired blind endpoint differences, use circular moving-block bootstrap (20,000 replicates, block length 7, seed 890027) for 95% percentile confidence intervals and circular block sign-flip randomization (20,000 replicates, block length 7, seed 890028) for p-values; apply Holm across the three endpoint p-values. Top5 is the single primary endpoint; Top10/Top20 are secondary. Also report uniform rank baseline (Top5=0.125, Top10=0.25, Top20=0.5, mean rank=20.5) descriptively.
frozen_candidate_selection.selected_candidate_ledger: Second-pass prior-only ranking for the two frozen candidate formula IDs on every blind target; record target/cutoff/actual quintet, formula IDs, five actual-number ranks per formula, Top5/Top10/Top20 hit counts and rank sums. Reconcile row-by-row to the canonical archive.
frozen_candidate_selection.leakage_guard: Candidate IDs must be frozen using Discovery and Validation only. The blind target ledger and paired inference are computed only after the IDs are frozen; no blind formula ranking or blind result may alter selection.

acceptance_gates: Q88 refreshed outputs on the same canonical archive pass aggregate acceptance, byte-exact persistence readback, and current exact-head CI before Q89 dispatch.
All 15 deterministic shard manifests cover formula ranks 0..4686824 exactly once with no gaps, overlaps, or duplicate formula IDs.
Each chronological split has exactly 4686825 formula rows; total metric row count is 14060475 and primary p-value count is exactly 42181425.

Target ledger contains 3351 unique chronological targets from 2017-09-05 through 2026-11-07; every target date, actual quintet, immediate prior cutoff and prior_draws count reconcile to canonical archive.
Strict-prefix/no-target-leakage checks pass for every target; state updates occur only after target scoring.
Selected nine-feature and eight-feature candidate IDs are derived only from Discovery/Validation by the frozen rule; second-pass blind ledger reconciles all 670 targets and both frozen formulas.
Global Holm family and paired blind bootstrap/sign-flip inference are reproducible from persisted code, seed, ledger and manifest.
All report, manifest, chunked metrics, target ledger, selected-candidate ledger, queue status and checkpoint are persisted append-only through Git Data API and reread byte-for-byte.
Exact-head CI passes on the persisted commit. Q89 remains VALIDATED_PENDING_HUMAN_REVIEW; it cannot be marked COMPLETE until human review/integration is recorded.
known_limitations: Finite nine-feature equal-weight subset grammar only; weighted, conditional, nonlinear, arbitrary formulas and feature definitions outside the registered 27 remain open.
Retrospective best-per-target formulas are descriptive and not ex-ante forecasts.
The formula-family p-values use a continuity-corrected normal approximation to a finite-population null; they are exploratory, not exact.
The historical blind tail has been inspected repeatedly by the broader SONAR project and is not independent project-level confirmation.

A large exhaustive catalog creates selection-overfit risk even with global Holm; the frozen Discovery→Validation→Blind candidate procedure is a separate guardrail, not evidence of lottery predictability.
